name: Decembrist revolt
title: The story of the Decembrist revolt

text: More than 200 years ago, some Russian army officers had fought in the Napoleonic Wars and seen peasant soldiers suffer.
They formed secret groups to end serfdom, the system that kept peasants bound to landowners.
src: Officers who had seen the Napoleonic Wars and the suffering of peasant soldiers formed secret societies from 1816
seeking a constitution and the end of serfdom / the abolition of serfdom with the land kept by the landlords

text: They also wanted a constitution, a set of rules so the emperor, called the tsar, could no longer rule alone.
In 1825 Tsar Alexander I died suddenly, and there was confusion over who would rule next.
src: The Decembrists wanted to replace the autocracy of the Russian Empire with a constitutional order
In the confusion after Alexander I’s death in 1825 / Alexander I dies suddenly

text: In December 1825, about 3,000 rebel soldiers gathered in Senate Square in Saint Petersburg and refused to obey Nicholas I.
Their leader never came, and at the end of the day loyal troops fired big guns and scattered them.
src: About 3,000 rebel troops refuse the oath to Nicholas I in Senate Square, Saint Petersburg / the rising in Senate Square in December 1825
Prince Sergei Trubetskoy, deserted it on the day / loyal troops broke them with grapeshot at the end of the day / are scattered by artillery

text: Five leaders were hanged, and many others were sent far away to Siberia.
Many of their wives gave up their comfortable lives to follow them there.
src: Five leaders were hanged, and many other participants were imprisoned or exiled to Siberia
The wives of many Decembrists, and some sisters and nieces, gave up privilege and comfort to follow them into exile

text: In Siberia the Decembrists started schools and brought new crops, such as rye, buckwheat and barley.
In 1856 the new tsar, Alexander II, pardoned them and gave back their rights.
src: they founded many schools for native people / they introduced crops such as vegetables, tobacco, rye, buckwheat and barley
On 26 August 1856, on the accession of Alexander II, the Decembrists were amnestied and their rights restored

text: The poet Alexander Pushkin wrote poems to his Decembrist friends, and Leo Tolstoy began a novel about them.
Their revolt is remembered as the beginning of the struggle for change in Russia.
src: Alexander Pushkin addressed poems to Decembrist friends / Leo Tolstoy began a novel about them
the revolt has been considered the beginning of a revolutionary movement in Russia
